description: Hit Rate@k comparing hybrid_search() (dense+BM25+RRF) against dense_search() (Qdrant-alone) on the 33 of 39 eval cases that are answerable with a defined expected keyword (unanswerable cases excluded - no fact to check retrieval against). A hit means every expected keyword for that case appears somewhere in the top-k retrieved chunks, checked before any LLM synthesis happens.

differing_cases.question: What was the enterprise revenue growth percentage?
What was SMB revenue this quarter?
Why did expenses stay flat this quarter?
What was net revenue retention this quarter?
How big is the engineering team?
Why was the database migration delayed from its original Q2 target?
Is engineering headcount consistent between the business review and the infrastructure report?
How much money did the company make in Q3?
How big is the engineering team?
Are there any tech debt concerns?

note: Production uses top_k=5 (app/agent/graph.py), where hybrid and dense-only tie at 100%. At tighter k the two methods trade wins and losses with no consistent winner - see conversation for the follow-up investigation into whether a test set designed to favor hybrid changes this.
